# {{project.name}}

> Reactive, compiler-free Custom Elements powered by `@beforesemicolon/markup` and native Web Component standards.

Package: `{{project.name}}`
Version: `{{project.version}}`
Documentation: https://web-component.beforesemicolon.com/documentation/
Complete context: https://web-component.beforesemicolon.com/llms-full.txt

Use this file as the authoritative compact contract when generating code with `@beforesemicolon/web-component`. Do not substitute React component conventions, JSX, decorators, or framework-specific lifecycle APIs.

## Before Semicolon ecosystem

The packages form one composable browser ecosystem:

1. `@beforesemicolon/markup` owns reactive `html` templates, `state`, `effect`, refs, and helpers.
2. `@beforesemicolon/web-component` owns Custom Elements, reactive props and component state, lifecycle hooks, styles, events, refs, and form integration. It re-exports all Markup APIs.
3. `@beforesemicolon/router` owns URL routing, navigation, route guards, route data, and route-aware Custom Elements.
4. `@beforesemicolon/intl` owns locale scopes, message loading, translations, and internationalized formatting.

When an application already imports `@beforesemicolon/web-component`, import `html`, `state`, `effect`, and Markup helpers from that package. A separate direct Markup dependency is normally unnecessary.

Router and Intl are complementary packages built on Web Component. They do not replace component state or Markup rendering, and they may be installed together.

Canonical ecosystem documentation:

- https://markup.beforesemicolon.com/llms.txt
- https://router.beforesemicolon.com/llms.txt
- https://intl.beforesemicolon.com/llms.txt

## Installation and exports

```bash
npm install @beforesemicolon/web-component
```

```javascript
import {
    WebComponent,
    html,
    css,
    state,
    effect,
    when,
    repeat,
} from '@beforesemicolon/web-component'
```

`WebComponent`, `HTMLComponentElement`, `css`, and component types are owned here. The templating APIs are re-exported from `@beforesemicolon/markup`.

Direct browser usage:

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/@beforesemicolon/web-component/dist/client.js"></script>
<script>
    const { WebComponent, css } = BFS
    const { html, state, effect, when, repeat } = BFS.MARKUP
</script>
```

## Component shape

```typescript
import { WebComponent, html, css } from '@beforesemicolon/web-component'

interface CounterProps {
    label: string
}

interface CounterState {
    count: number
}

class CounterButton extends WebComponent<CounterProps, CounterState> {
    static observedAttributes = ['label']

    label = 'Count'
    initialState = { count: 0 }

    stylesheet = css`
        :host {
            display: inline-block;
        }
    `

    increment = () => {
        const count = this.state.count() + 1
        this.setState({ count })
        this.dispatch('count-change', { count })
    }

    render() {
        return html`
            <button type="button" onclick="${this.increment}">
                ${this.props.label}: ${this.state.count}
            </button>
        `
    }
}

customElements.define('counter-button', CounterButton)
```

Use a hyphenated Custom Element name. `render` may return a Markup `HtmlTemplate`, a string, a DOM node, or nothing.

## Props and state

- Put public attributes in `static observedAttributes` using kebab-case.
- Define each prop's default as a camel-case class field.
- Read reactive props through `this.props.name`, which is a Markup state getter.
- Put component-owned values in `initialState`.
- Read reactive state through `this.state.name`.
- Call `this.setState(partial)` or `this.setState(previous => partial)` only after mounting.
- Return new object and array references rather than mutating state in place.

```javascript
class UserPanel extends WebComponent {
    static observedAttributes = ['display-name']
    displayName = 'Guest'
    initialState = { expanded: false }

    toggle = () => {
        this.setState(({ expanded }) => ({ expanded: !expanded }))
    }

    render() {
        return html`
            <button aria-expanded="${this.state.expanded}" onclick="${this.toggle}">
                ${this.props.displayName}
            </button>
        `
    }
}
```

Pass getters directly to template interpolation to keep them reactive. Calling `this.state.expanded()` before interpolation creates a snapshot.

## Lifecycle contract

- `onMount()` runs after the initial render and may return one cleanup function.
- `onUpdate(name, newValue, oldValue)` responds to observed prop changes.
- `onDestroy()` runs when the element disconnects, after the mount cleanup.
- `onAdoption()` runs when the element moves to another document.
- `onError(error)` receives rendering and lifecycle errors; the default logs them.

```javascript
onMount() {
    const onResize = () => this.setState({ width: window.innerWidth })
    window.addEventListener('resize', onResize)
    return () => window.removeEventListener('resize', onResize)
}
```

Do not call native lifecycle callbacks directly or override them as public extension points.

## Refs and DOM roots

Use `ref` for elements owned by the component template:

```javascript
render() {
    return html`<input ref="search" type="search" />`
}

onMount() {
    const [input] = this.refs.search ?? []
    input?.focus()
}
```

- `this.refs` is the rendered Markup template's live ref map.
- `this.contentRoot` is the Shadow Root by default, or the host when shadow DOM is disabled.
- `this.root` is the closest document or Shadow Root containing the component.
- Refs exist only while their elements are mounted.

## Events

`this.dispatch(name, detail)` creates a `CustomEvent` whose payload is available at `event.detail`.

```javascript
this.dispatch('save', { id: '42' })
```

Consumers use native event listeners. Do not assume events bubble or cross a shadow boundary unless the component implements those options itself.

## Styling

Assign `stylesheet` a CSS string, `CSSStyleSheet`, or reactive `css` result:

```javascript
stylesheet = css`
    :host {
        color: ${() => (this.props.tone() === 'danger' ? 'crimson' : 'inherit')};
    }
`
```

Shadow DOM is enabled by default. Set `config = { ...this.config, shadow: false }` only when the component intentionally renders into its host.

## Router and Intl composition

Install only the capabilities the application needs:

```bash
npm install @beforesemicolon/web-component @beforesemicolon/router @beforesemicolon/intl
```

```javascript
import { WebComponent, html } from '@beforesemicolon/web-component'
import '@beforesemicolon/router'
import '@beforesemicolon/intl'
```

```html
<page-route path="/orders/:orderId">
    <intl-locale locale="en-US" src-dir="/locales">
        <h1><intl-msg key="orders.title">Orders</intl-msg></h1>
        <intl-number type="currency" currency="USD">129.99</intl-number>
    </intl-locale>
</page-route>
```

In direct browser mode, load Web Component before Router or Intl because both require `BFS.MARKUP` and `BFS.WebComponent`.

## Rules for generated code

- Use standard HTML attributes and lowercase event attributes, not JSX syntax.
- Import Markup APIs from Web Component when Web Component is already the app foundation.
- Keep `render` declarative and put subscriptions, timers, and DOM side effects in lifecycle hooks.
- Use props for externally controlled inputs and state for component-owned values.
- Use native Custom Elements registration and native event consumption.
- Read the Router contract before generating routes and the Intl contract before generating localization code.
